articles.title: Why your Next.js SSE stream arrives as one blob (and the settings that fix it)
articles.excerpt: Your route logs tokens flowing out one at a time. The browser shows nothing — then the entire answer appears at once, as if it were never a stream at all. The model is streaming fine; something betwee…
articles.body: Your route logs tokens flowing out one at a time. The browser shows nothing — then the entire answer appears at once, as if it were never a stream at all. The model is streaming fine; something between your route handler and the browser is holding the bytes back and releasing them in a single flush. It is almost always one of three things, and none of them show up on localhost. The response headers that stop a proxy from buffering An SSE response has to tell every hop between your server and the browser to pass bytes through untouched.

articles.title: I gave my agent a broken JSON.parse — did it spot the trailing comma?
articles.excerpt: I built a small tool to test my own AI agent in 10 minutes, instead of trusting that it "looked right." One test from it: "Find the JSON bug." The prompt is a single line: const settings = JSON.parse(…
articles.body: I built a small tool to test my own AI agent in 10 minutes, instead of trusting that it "looked right." One test from it: "Find the JSON bug." The prompt is a single line: const settings = JSON.parse('{"theme":"dark",}'); That trailing comma after "dark" is invalid JSON, so JSON.parse fails. The check is simple: name the trailing comma as the cause, show the smallest valid fix, and explain it. I ran two answers through it: A good answer — "The trailing comma after \"dark\" is invalid JSON. Fix: JSON.parse('{\"theme\":\"dark\"}')" — scored 4/4. What-to-fix: "No fix needed for this task." A weak answer — "The JSON is broken because the theme value is wrong. Fix: change dark to light." — scored 3/4. It lost the "Is correct" point, because it never named the real cause.

articles.body: Five loader domains in 15 months: using rotation and parking to guide monitoring The Magento loader campaign has changed infrastructure repeatedly. Sansec tracked the first domain, manulfie.click , from July 2025, then neswnsssn.click , lanhd6549tdhse.top , additionalver.com , and the current deepveindrilling.com . The report associates the domains with 863, 494, 355, 246, and 83 stores, respectively, and says the group has hit 953 stores overall. The difference between the per-domain totals and the campaign total reflects overlapping victims. Domain rotation creates a common monitoring problem. A block on the newest domain may stop a fresh request, but the store can still contain an older script, and a visitor who previously received a payload may retain it in localStorage.

articles.body: From struggling with YAML indentation to scoring 84% on the Certified Kubernetes Application Developer exam in just one month. On November 5, 2026, I passed the Certified Kubernetes Application Developer (CKAD) exam with a score of 84% . One month earlier, I was struggling with a seemingly simple exercise: deploying a multi-container Redis Pod using a ConfigMap and an emptyDir volume. I was fighting YAML indentation errors and trying to understand how volumes and mounts actually worked together. What made the difference wasn't studying more theory. My one-month preparation plan. My practice exam scores.

articles.title: Comment laisser Claude Code lire les checks GitNest et proposer une relance que vous validez dans osFoundry
articles.excerpt: À la fin de ce guide, vous pouvez demander à Claude Code « le change set de checkout est-il au vert ? » et obtenir une réponse lue depuis osFoundry, pas devinée à partir de vos tests locaux. Claude Co…
articles.body: À la fin de ce guide, vous pouvez demander à Claude Code « le change set de checkout est-il au vert ? » et obtenir une réponse lue depuis osFoundry , pas devinée à partir de vos tests locaux. Claude Code liste les checks du commit composé du change set, vous dit lequel a échoué et, s'il semble instable (flaky), demande une relance pour ce seul check. La relance ne démarre pas quand Claude Code la demande. Elle arrive dans osFoundry sous forme de carte « Retry GitNest check » portant la version du change set et le commit exact, et ne s'exécute que lorsque vous cliquez sur Approve retry.

articles.body: A satellite looks down at the International Space Station in orbit. (Image credit: HEO) A commercial satellite has spotted the International Space Station (ISS), giving us a unique view of the orbiting lab from above. What is it? Most of the time, when we see the ISS, it is from down here on Earth or from the viewpoint of the astronauts onboard, peering out the windows at the station's limbs, solar arrays and instruments. But in this snapshot, which was posted on X on Nov. 9 by the Australian company HEO, we can see the station stretched out in all its glory. HEO specializes in using satellites in low Earth orbit to capture images of other spacecraft, though longer-term the company aims to capture observations far out into the solar system.

articles.body: I’ve spent a lot of time with smart telescopes , from relatively inexpensive Seestar models to the original Vaonis Vespera and the Vespera Pro . They all promise essentially the same thing — you put a telescope outside at night, choose something interesting on your smartphone and let the technology take care of the rest. The Vaonis Vespera 3 does that exceptionally well, but after spending several nights with it, I’m convinced it’s designed for a rather different kind of buyer. The telescope’s optical arm folds into its curved body when switched off. (Image credit: Jamie Carter) At $2,490/£2,199, this is hardly an impulse purchase for the beginner who’s curious about astronomy – you could buy several perfectly capable smart telescopes for the same money.

articles.body: Ancient Egyptian temples will inevitably dominate the story of the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 . After all, the path of totality crosses Luxor, home to Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, and some of the ancient world's most famous monuments. But follow the moon 's shadow west and another ancient civilization comes into view. Before reaching Egypt, totality will sweep across the Mediterranean and North Africa, passing over an extraordinary collection of Roman cities, fortresses, theaters, temples and triumphal arches. Many lie within what became Rome's North African provinces, a region that produced some of the empire's wealthiest and most impressive cities.

articles.title: Astronomers stunned after James Webb Space Telescope discovers the earliest pair of black hole-powered quasars
articles.excerpt: Using the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist!
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have discovered the oldest pair of supermassive black hole-powered quasars ever seen. There's just one problem: they shouldn't exist! The compact quasar pair, spotted with the aid of the Gemini North telescope, has been designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, which means "Two celestial bodies of fathomless powerful darkness in the brilliance of heat reincarnating energy into the universe." The compact quasar pair is seen as it was 900 million years after the Big Bang at a time when such supermassive black holes should not have had time to grow to such tremendous masses. Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua isn't just the oldest and most distant quasar pairing ever seen.
